1.name: RO
1.hint: receiver output, high impedance while RE is high (p. 7); high when A − B ≥ 200 mV, low when ≤ −200 mV, high with both inputs open (p. 12); VOH ≥ VCC − 0.4 V at 1.5 mA

2.name: RE#
2.hint: receiver output enable, active low; RE high with DE low enters shutdown (p. 7)

3.name: DE
3.hint: driver output enable, active high (p. 7); no internal pull is stated – a floating DE at reset leaves the bus undefined

6.name: A
6.hint: non-inverting receiver input and driver output; bus pin: absolute maximum −7.5 V … +12.5 V; receiver specified for −7 V ≤ VCM ≤ 12 V; input resistance ≥ 12 kΩ (32 transceivers per bus); driver high impedance while DE is low

7.name: B
7.hint: inverting receiver input and driver output; bus pin: absolute maximum −7.5 V … +12.5 V; receiver specified for −7 V ≤ VCM ≤ 12 V; input resistance ≥ 12 kΩ (32 transceivers per bus); driver high impedance while DE is low

hints: 3.3 V part: VCC 3.0–3.6 V (p. 7); the logic inputs DE, RE, DI take up to 7 V ('interoperable with +5V logic', p. 1–2), RO swings to VCC; the MAX485 is the 5 V counterpart with the same pinout

RS-485 bus: terminate the line at both ends in its characteristic impedance and keep stubs short (Figures 21–22 show 120 Ω at each end); the data sheet names no fail-safe bias for an idle terminated bus – its receiver fail-safe covers open inputs only (p. 14)
half duplex, up to 10 Mbps, drivers not slew-rate limited (p. 1); RE high and DE low for at least 300 ns enters shutdown, 2 nA typ. (p. 3, p. 5, p. 12)
driver short-circuit current up to ±250 mA at −7 V / 12 V; thermal shutdown releases the driver outputs (p. 3, p. 14)
idd_max_a 2.2 mA is the no-load supply current with DE high (p. 3); a driver into a terminated bus draws its load current on top

pin description, p. 7; pin configuration (TOP VIEW), p. 8

pin v_max_v 7.3 on RO: VCC + 0.3 V at the absolute maximum VCC 7 V (computed from p. 2)

function tables and applications, p. 12; termination, p. 14
